text:
You grade one workflow job of Rho-Bank's procedure library against an answer key. An answering
agent serves customers by following this job exactly, as it is shown below (its steps, conditions,
arguments, rules and the facts it asks for; the quotes behind them are not shown to the agent).
For each fact in the key, decide whether the job leads the agent to it; for each trap, decide
whether the job tells the agent to do it. Judge only what the job says, not what a good agent
would know without it.

Facts:
- right: a step, an argument or a rule leads the agent to the fact for every case the fact names.
- partly: it does for some of the cases the fact names and is silent on the others, or it says
  it so loosely that an agent following it could give another answer.
- missing: nothing in the job leads the agent to it; the agent would have to work it out alone.
- wrong: the job leads the agent to a different answer for at least one case the fact names, even
  if it is right for others.

Traps:
- present: a step, an argument or a rule tells the agent to do it, for some case.
- absent: nothing in the job does.

Then list the conflicts: two steps, arguments or rules that give the same case different
instructions, so an agent could follow either.

Job: pin_lock_investigation_protocol

{
 "job": "pin_lock_investigation_protocol",
 "when": {},
 "starts": {
  "by": "customer",
  "note": "customer: only when the customer reports a debit card that was declined or locked because of the PIN (CODE 55, 75 or 83). The agent then investigates every locked card before unlocking any of them. Closure, replacement, disputes, a PIN reset or a security-team transfer are offered only on the paths the protocol names, and are carried out only if the customer accepts. The one exception is 3+ prior locks: there the protocol requires a PIN reset instead of an unlock."
 },

  },

   "tool": "order_debit_card_5739",
   "who": "agent",
   "step": null,
   "not_used": "This job does not order cards. The replacement runs in the replacement-order procedure."
  }
 ],
 "info": [
  {
   "field": "identity_values",
   "about": "Any 2 of date of birth, email, phone number and address, checked against the records",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "To verify your identity, could you please provide two of the following: your date of birth, email, phone number, or address on file?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "locked_cards",
   "about": "Which debit cards or checking accounts the customer says are locked. These are confirmed against the records, and every checking account is looked up.",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "Which of your Rho-Bank debit cards are being declined, and which one would you like to start with?",
   "may_hold_back": false
  },
  {
   "field": "decline_description",
   "about": "What the decline said (PIN locked, incorrect PIN, unable to verify PIN) and where it happened",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "What message did you see when the card was declined, and where were you using it?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "decline_circumstances",
   "about": "The customer's own account of each locked card: where they were, roughly when, and what amount they tried. Do not reveal the record first.",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "Can you tell me what happened when this card was locked? Where were you, roughly what time was it, and what amount were you trying to spend or withdraw?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "card_status_fields",
   "about": "For each card: pin_locked, pin_lock_reason, pin_attempts_remaining, status, issue_reason, date_issued, daily_atm_limit, card_number_last_4, prior PIN locks in the last 90 days, fraud_alert_active, velocity_blocked",
   "from": "records",
   "ask": null,
   "may_hold_back": false
  },
  {
   "field": "declined_transactions",
   "about": "For each account: transactions of type atm_withdrawal_declined or pos_declined, with their city, time, amount and spacing. Also the successful transactions of the last 7 days, the usual ATM withdrawal, overdraft fees and the balance.",
   "from": "records",
   "ask": null,
   "may_hold_back": false
  },
  {
   "field": "customer_location_time_confirmation",
   "about": "Whether the customer was at the location and time of the declined attempt",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "I see your card was locked after failed PIN attempts at [location from transaction]. Were you at that location? / These attempts occurred at [time]. Were you trying to use your card at that time?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "amount_confirmation",
   "about": "Whether the customer tried the declined amounts (asked only when the amount-pattern flag scored)",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "The attempts were for [amount 1], then [amount 2], then [amount 3]. Do you remember trying those specific amounts?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "attempts_were_yours",
   "about": "For a medium score: whether the failed PIN attempts were the customer's own",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "I see failed PIN attempts on your card. Were those attempts yours?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "unauthorized_confirmation",
   "about": "Whether each successful transaction in the suspicious period was the customer's own",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "I see a [amount] transaction at [merchant] on [date]. Did you make this transaction?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "cannot_unlock_choice",
   "about": "For a card that cannot be unlocked: which of the offered options the customer wants",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "For your protection I can't unlock this card. I can close it and send a replacement with a new number, transfer you to our security team, or reset your PIN. Which would you like?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "transfer_accepted",
   "about": "Whether the customer wants a transfer to the security team for a card on security hold, and whether to finish other cards first",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "This card needs our security team. Would you like me to transfer you to them for this card, and should we finish your other cards first?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  }
 ],
 "steps": [
  {
   "id": "identify",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Look up the customer by name, email or id, using whichever they gave. Ask for 2 of: date of birth, email, phone, address. Compare them with the record.",
   "call": "get_user_information_by_name",
   "args": {
    "customer_name": "the name the customer gave (or use get_user_information_by_email / get_user_information_by_id with what they gave)"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "check_identity",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Confirm that at least 2 of the values match the record from identify. Share no card or account information before they match. If they still do not match after asking again, tell the customer you cannot verify them and stop.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "identify"
   ],
   "after": [
    "identify"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "time",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Get the current time. It is the timestamp for the verification log, and the 'now' that the card-history and transaction counts in score are measured to.",
   "call": "get_current_time",
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "check_identity"
   ],
   "if": "the customer's identity was verified in check_identity"
  },
  {
   "id": "log_verif",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Record the verification with log_verification, using the record's values and the time from the time step.",
   "call": "log_verification",
   "args": {
    "name": "verified user's name",
    "user_id": "verified user id",
    "address": "record address",
    "email": "record email",
    "phone_number": "record phone",
    "date_of_birth": "record DOB (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "time_verified": "time from get_current_time"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "check_identity"
   ],
   "after": [
    "time"
   ],
   "if": "the customer's identity was verified in check_identity"
  },
  {
   "id": "accounts",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 with unlock_discoverable_agent_tool, then call it with call_discoverable_agent_tool. Note each checking account's account_id, account_class, status, balance and date_opened.",
   "call": "get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847",
   "args": {
    "user_id": "the verified user"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "log_verif"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "cards",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823, then call it once for each checking account from accounts. For each card, read card_id, card_number_last_4, status, issue_reason, date_issued, daily_atm_limit, pin_locked, pin_attempts_remaining, pin_lock_reason, prior PIN locks, fraud_alert_active and velocity_blocked. If the reply says an account is not a checking account, skip it: only checking accounts have debit cards.",
   "call": "get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823",
   "args": {
    "account_id": "each checking account id from accounts"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "accounts"
   ],
   "after": [
    "accounts"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "txns",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock get_bank_account_transactions_9173, then call it once for each account that has a locked card. Read the declined attempts and the recent successful activity.",
   "call": "get_bank_account_transactions_9173",
   "args": {
    "account_id": "each checking account with a locked card"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked = TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_which_card",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If several cards are affected, ask which one the customer wants to discuss first and take them in that order. If another card on the same account also has pin_locked TRUE, finish investigating all of those cards (check_other_locked) before unlocking any of them.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "more than one of the customer's cards is declined or locked"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_circumstances",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, you may ask the customer what happened: where they were, roughly when, and what amount they tried. Never reveal the scoring. Score the card from the card data and the declined transactions in txns. Use the customer's answers through the Step 4 questions (ask_location, ask_time, ask_amount) and the threshold questions; those questions may name the location, time and amounts from the records.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "txns"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked TRUE and the customer has not yet described how it was locked"
  },
  {
   "id": "not_locked_branch",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the card's pin_locked is FALSE but pin_attempts_remaining is low, tell the customer how many attempts remain before the card locks. If they have forgotten the PIN, offer a PIN reset.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "the card's pin_locked is FALSE and pin_attempts_remaining is low"
  },
  {
   "id": "code_83_branch",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the decline was a PIN verification or network error (CODE 83) and the card is not locked, explain that the PIN was not wrong and advise retrying. If it keeps failing, suggest a signature transaction, a different terminal or merchant, or waiting 10-15 minutes.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "the decline was 'unable to verify PIN' (CODE 83) and pin_locked is FALSE"
  },
  {
   "id": "triggers",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, check the automatic triggers first. A security_hold card cannot be unlocked here; it goes to the security-hold transfer offer. If another card on the same account also has pin_locked TRUE, investigate all of those cards before any unlock. If a card on the account was replaced as stolen in the last 90 days, enhanced verification is required.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "txns",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "txns"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "check_security_hold",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, read pin_lock_reason. If it is 'security_hold', do not score or unlock the card. Offer to transfer the customer to the security team for that card, and keep handling the customer's other cards normally.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "security_hold_transfer",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the customer accepts the offer, call transfer_to_human_agents with reason fraud_or_security_concern and a summary of the customer's issue and what was attempted. If other locked cards are still being handled, first ask the customer whether they want to finish those cards before the transfer, and follow their answer.",
   "call": "transfer_to_human_agents",
   "args": {
    "summary": "the customer's issue (the card with pin_lock_reason security_hold) and what was attempted or done for the customer's cards",
    "reason": "fraud_or_security_concern"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "after": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "if": "pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold' AND the customer accepts the transfer offer"
  },
  {
   "id": "security_hold_declined",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the customer declines the transfer, acknowledge it and do not unlock the card. A security hold is an automatic escalation trigger, so you may follow check_unauthorized and cannot_unlock_options for that card: closure and replacement, or a PIN reset, with the transfer still available. You may tell them they can contact Rho-Bank later about that card. Close the conversation politely once the other cards are done.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "after": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "if": "pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold' AND the customer declines the transfer"
  },
  {
   "id": "check_other_locked",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If another card on the same account as a locked card also has pin_locked TRUE, finish investigating and scoring all of those cards before unlocking any of them. Each card gets its own score and outcome.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "another card on the same account also has pin_locked TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "check_recent_stolen",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Check whether any card on the account has issue_reason 'stolen' with a date_issued no more than 90 days before the current time. If one does, enhanced verification is required before an unlock. The documents give no tool for enhanced verification, so tell the customer the card cannot be unlocked in this chat. Because this is an automatic escalation trigger, follow check_unauthorized and cannot_unlock_options for the card.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "a card on the account has issue_reason 'stolen' and a date_issued no more than 90 days before the current time"
  },
  {
   "id": "score",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Score each card that has no security hold and no recent-stolen trigger, using flags A1-A3, B1-B3, C1-C4, D1-D3 and E1-E3. 'Last 7 days' runs from 7 days before the current time (time step) to the current time. 'Last 90 days' runs from 90 days before the current time to the current time. Card age is measured from date_issued to the current time, and account age from date_opened to the current time. Never reveal the calculation.\nA1: city of the declined attempt vs the address city. Same city 0, other city in the same state 1, other state 2, other country 3.\nA2: 2 locations 1, 3+ locations 2.\nA3: +1 if all successful transactions in the last 7 days were in the home city but the declines are elsewhere.\nB1: hour of the attempt. 6AM-10PM 0, 10PM-12AM 1, 12-2AM 2, 2-6AM 3.\nB2: last successful PIN use 7-30 days ago 1, over 30 days ago 2.\nB3: gap between failed attempts. 2-5 min 1, 1-2 min 2, under 1 min 3.\nC1: decreasing amounts 2.\nC2: all round hundreds 1.\nC3: 2-5x the average successful ATM withdrawal 1, over 5x 2.\nC4: 80-100% of daily_atm_limit 1, attempts totalling over the limit 2.\nD1: prior locks in the last 90 days. 1 scores 1, 2 scores 2, 3+ scores 3.\nD2: card age 1-3 months 1, under 1 month 2.\nD3: another card with a velocity block +1, with a fraud alert +2.\nE1: account age 3-6 months 1, under 3 months 2.\nE2: 1 overdraft fee 1, 2+ fees 2.\nE3: balance $50-100 1, under $50 2.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "txns",
    "accounts",
    "identify",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers",
    "check_security_hold",
    "check_other_locked",
    "check_recent_stolen"
   ],
   "if": "pin_lock_reason is not 'security_hold' and no card on the account was replaced as stolen within 90 days before the current time"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_location",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the score is 5 or higher and the Location Mismatch flag (A1) scored, ask whether the customer was at the location of the declined attempt. If yes, remove the location flags and rescore. If no, keep the score and proceed with caution.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "score >= 5 and A1 (Location Mismatch) scored"
  },
  {
   "id": "foreign_location_denied",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the declines were in a different country (A1 = 3) and the customer says they were not there, keep the location flags. If the customer also answers the time question with 'I was asleep' or similar, the card is CRITICAL: do not unlock it. Go to check_unauthorized, then recommend closure and replacement (cannot_unlock_options). This holds even if the customer still has the physical card.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "ask_location"
   ],
   "if": "A1 is a different country and the customer denies being at that location"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_time",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the score is 5 or higher and the time-of-day flag scored 2 or more, ask whether the customer was using the card at that time. If they confirm, remove the time flag. If they say they were asleep or similar, treat the card as CRITICAL (likely fraud).",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "score >= 5 and time-of-day flag >= 2"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_amount",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the score is 5 or higher and the amount-pattern flag (C1) scored, read back the attempted amounts and ask whether the customer remembers them. If they confirm, remove the flag. If they deny it or seem confused, keep it.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "score >= 5 and amount pattern flag (C1) scored"
  },
  {
   "id": "velocity_flag_stays",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "B3 scores 3 when consecutive failed attempts are less than 1 minute apart. Step 4 gives questions only for the Location Mismatch, Amount Pattern and Time of Day flags. It gives no question or answer that removes B3, so B3 keeps its 3 points even when the customer says the attempts were theirs. A 3-point flag goes to single_flag_escalation, which leads to check_unauthorized and cannot_unlock_options. You may explain that the pattern of the attempts triggered a security review, without revealing the scoring.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "the card's consecutive failed attempts were less than 1 minute apart (B3 = 3)"
  },
  {
   "id": "medium_question",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For a final score of 5-7, ask: 'I see failed PIN attempts on your card. Were those attempts yours?' Once it has been asked, the card may be unlocked (unlock_handoff). If the customer says the attempts were not theirs, no passage withholds the unlock at this level. Tell them so, and ask whether they want the unlock or would rather change the PIN because someone may know it.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "ask_location",
    "ask_amount"
   ],
   "after": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount"
   ],
   "if": "the card's recalculated score is 5-7"
  },
  {
   "id": "decide",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Apply the thresholds to each card. 0-4: unlock. 5-7: unlock only after asking whether the attempts were the customer's. 8-10: unlock only if the customer confirms and gives a satisfactory explanation. 11-14: no unlock on this call. 15+, or a customer who says they were asleep at an overnight attempt: CRITICAL; do not unlock, follow check_unauthorized, then recommend closure and replacement (cannot_unlock_options). 3+ prior locks: a PIN reset instead of an unlock.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount",
    "medium_question"
   ],
   "after": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount",
    "medium_question"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "three_plus_locks_reset",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the card had 3 or more prior PIN locks in the 90 days before the current time, do not unlock it. Tell the customer that, because the card has been locked several times recently, it cannot simply be unlocked and needs a new PIN. Run the PIN reset (unlock_and_post_unlock_pin_reset) for that card. D1 at 3 points is a single 3-point flag, so single_flag_escalation also applies. If the card meets another cannot-unlock condition, follow check_unauthorized and cannot_unlock_options as well. Never reveal the scoring.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "score",
    "decide"
   ],
   "after": [

## The answer key

- K1 (overnight_denial): declined attempts in another US state between 2 AM and 6 AM that the customer denies, saying she was asleep at home, make the card CRITICAL (likely fraud): it is not unlocked, whatever the total; the job reaches this for a different state, not only for a different country
- K2 (critical_outcome): a CRITICAL card with no successful unauthorized transaction is recommended for closure and replacement because fraud is suspected, and on the customer's yes it is closed and a replacement ordered for the same checking account (the closing and the order may run in the jobs this one names)
- K3 (suspicious_period): the suspicious period checked for successful unauthorized transactions is the window of the declined attempts the customer denies (from the first of them to now): successful transactions before it, her usual home-city activity, are not put to her as possibly unauthorized and not disputed, so a card whose period holds only declined attempts gets no dispute and she is told no money was taken
- K4 (admitted_attempts): a card whose declined attempts the customer confirms were hers (at that store, at that time, for that amount: she mixed up PINs) has its location flags removed and its score recalculated, and with no 3-point flag, fewer than 3 prior locks and a recalculated score of 10 or less it is cleared for unlock: not closed, not escalated, not sent to the cannot-unlock options
- K5 (card_order): locked cards on different checking accounts are taken one at a time, in the order the customer chooses, each to its outcome before the next is investigated; the trigger to finish investigating every locked card before any unlock applies only to locked cards on the same checking account
- K6 (two_prior_locks): a card cleared for unlock with 2 prior PIN locks in the last 90 days must be asked 'This is your third PIN lock in 90 days. Would you like me to reset your PIN to a new number?', and on a yes its PIN is reset to the new PIN the customer chooses (reset_debit_card_pin_6284, here or in the PIN-reset job this one names)
- K7 (security_hold): a card with pin_lock_reason security_hold is not scored, unlocked or reset: the agent offers a transfer to the security team, and when the customer declines it does nothing more on that card (no transfer, no write)

## The traps

- T1: every locked card the customer has, on any checking account, is investigated and scored before any of them is unlocked (the same-account trigger applied across accounts)
- T2: a PIN reset is offered, beside closure and a transfer, for a CRITICAL card (one whose overnight attempts the customer slept through); the reset clears the lock, so taking it unlocks a card that cannot be unlocked
- T4: the suspicious period reaches back before the first declined attempt the customer denies (to the last transaction she confirms as hers, or over the recent successful activity), so earlier home-city transactions she does not recognise are put to her and disputed
